title: IPC server (core/pkg/ipc): JSON-RPC 2.0 over Unix socket / named pipe
description:
## Background
Section 3.9: Core exposes JSON-RPC 2.0 IPC (Unix socket macOS/Linux, named pipe Windows) for UI-to-Core and plugin-to-Core. (Config manager and daemon lifecycle split out to sibling beads - see dependencies.)

## Reasoning
UI shell, script plugins, and Finder Sync extension all speak one protocol. Locking transport and framing before the shell scaffold and Level B runtime prevents three divergent ad-hoc protocols.

## Scope
- IPC server: JSON-RPC 2.0 over Unix socket / named pipe, bidirectional

## Pass criteria
- [ ] UI stub can call Core over IPC and get status (smoke test)
- [ ] Protocol documented (framing, error shapes, reconnect semantics); reconnect behavior covered by test
- [ ] Transport access restricted to the user (Unix-socket file mode / named-pipe ACL asserted in test) so another local user cannot inject commands

## Plan refs
Section 3.9 IPC Server.

title: Keyboard: declare the three headless kinds and bridge core.conflicts
description:
Three control kinds are registered, tested, and reachable from no daemon page. `app/frontend/src/controls/index.tsx` maps `conflictResolver` (:78), `keymapEditor` (:83) and `ruleBuilder` (:94); `remap.test.tsx` exercises them at `:526`, `:241` and `:389`; and NO Go page in `app/backend` declares any of them — grep over the Go pages for those kind strings returns nothing. The flagship "make it yours" flow, `RuleBuilderControl`'s full IF app / AND chord / THEN action sentence with Edit/Remove over `Service.UserRules`, is dead code.

They are reachable from a MOCK, which is exactly what makes the gap invisible. The e2e fixture declares all three on its own Shortcuts page (`app/frontend/src/test/fixtures.ts:206-208`) and `firstRun.test.tsx:180-255` drives the keymap editor, the rule builder and the conflict resolver end to end. The suite is therefore green against a fixture standing in for a page the daemon does not serve.

**The coverage gate cannot see this by construction.** `has a renderer for every kind a registered page declares` (renderers.test.tsx:301-314) asserts DECLARED is a subset of REGISTERED, never the reverse, so a kind that nothing declares fails no gate. That asymmetry is the argument for declaring these three by hand rather than waiting for a gate to ask, and it is why cross-os-tcd's Go guard is worth considering for the reverse direction too.

**The bridge that would make `conflictResolver` honest already exists daemon-side and is not bridged.** `core.conflicts` (registered `core/cmd/crossos/main.go:836`) serves, for every chord two still-firing rules claim: the rendered chord, the winner, the sorted loser rule ids, and each claimant's plugin and human action name — computed by compiling the candidate group into a real `event.Router` and calling `Decide` in each declared app context (`pagedata.go:1431-1468`; the compile/Decide loop at :1440-1446, the claimant rows at :1458-1465, `sort.Strings(row.Losers)` at :1466) — so the winner is exactly what the keyboard will pick. User-authored rules participate. The frontend instead reverse-derives conflicts from `Traces()` (`app/frontend/src/controls/ConflictResolver.tsx:56`), which means a collision is only visible for a chord the user has ALREADY pressed, and only within the last 200 recorded decisions. The collision worth warning about is the one that has not fired yet.

`config.getUserRuleVocabulary` (handler `userules.go:151`, registered `main.go:855`) returns `app_modes`, `app_categories`, `modifiers`, `keys`, `capabilities` and `actions` in one reply and has no bridge method, so every picker in the rule builder has no server vocabulary and the write hard-codes `app_modes: []` and `device_id: ""`.

Window chords in `ShortcutListControl` are typed as free text ("ctrl, shift") — the exact failure `ChordRecorder` was built to remove.
design:
Three changes, all small, no new daemon verbs: declare the kinds (ruleBuilder and keymapEditor on core.keyboard, conflictResolver alongside them), add Service.Conflicts + a ConflictRow type in app/backend/uisources.go, and add Service.UserRuleVocabulary. The daemon already serves all of it.

**Each bridge is more than one method, and one of them fails the build at COMPILE time.** For each of `Service.Conflicts` and `Service.UserRuleVocabulary` you need: a method on the `Core` interface (app/backend/bridge.go:64); a `stubCore` method (app/backend/shell_test.go:122) — skip this one and `go test` fails to build, not to assert; an `IPCCore` method (app/backend/ipc_client.go); an `App` method wrapping `a.core.X()` with `sourceList(a, "X", rows)` (bridge.go:366) so a null becomes `[]` and is logged, and `a.log.Append("X: " + err.Error())` on every error so "nothing is configured" never looks identical to "the daemon is gone"; a `Service` method (app/backend/service.go); a `ServiceApi` entry (app/frontend/src/types/controls.ts:397-446) AND a `controlSurface` entry (app/frontend/src/test/fixtures.ts:650) — `lib/service.ts` asserts the generated Wails Service against `ServiceApi` and `controlSurface` is annotated `: ServiceApi`, so either omission is a compile error; a row struct in app/backend/uisources.go; and an entry in the `shellCalls` list at `core/cmd/crossos/main_test.go:880` — which already names `core.conflicts` and `config.getUserRuleVocabulary`, so do NOT duplicate those; the comment there says "a method that is registered on neither list is reachable from neither."

`Service.UserRuleVocabulary` returns a `UserRuleVocabularyRow` with six slices whose ELEMENT TYPES this bead fixes rather than leaves to the implementer: `AppModes`, `AppCategories`, `Modifiers`, `Keys`, `Capabilities`, `Actions`. The daemon is the source of every value (handler `core/cmd/crossos/userules.go:151`, registered `main.go:855`) — mirror its element types exactly and do not reshape, dedupe or sort them in the shell, because a picker whose vocabulary disagrees with the validator it feeds produces a selection the daemon refuses. There is no device list in that reply and none is invented here: `device_id: ""` is the value `derive` reads as "claims no device", raising the rule's scope to Global or App (core/pkg/userrules/userrules.go:132-142), so the field is a declared non-dimension rather than a missing picker.

**Two spellings, one rule.** The page's control SOURCES are `core:keymapEditor` and `core:conflicts` (a colon) and are safe to write literally. A row action is a different thing: the "Turn off loser" control writes through `SetRuleEnabled`, and if you introduce an id for it, any `core.`-prefixed ACTION id must be assembled as `['core', '<verb>'].join('.')`, the convention actions.ts:41 and :58 already use. `config.getUserRuleVocabulary` is `config.`-prefixed and therefore never matched by the rule. Only ACTION ids use the dot.

**Reference discipline, stated against the table and not against the LICENSE file.** §9.11 has NO row for pqrs-org/Karabiner-Elements — its DATA ONLY row at `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md:1229` covers windows-keyboard-for-mac, karabiner-mac-to-windows and karabiner-windows-mode, three other repositories — so there is no §9.11 grade to lean on. The grade of record is `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md:1115`: study/adapt, Unlicense, and `third_party/Karabiner-Elements/LICENSE` is the public-domain dedication, which passes §9.11 (the gate rejects GPL, copyleft and unlicensed sources, and a dedication to the public domain is none of those). `third_party/Karabiner-Elements/ATTRIBUTION.md` already exists and already pins commit `c7197aaf27345c11a0d1e4bf9ddad0c9020ae387`, but it does not cover this port: its ComplexModificationsView.swift block records only the keyword-filter rule feeding KeymapEditorControl's search field, and its SearchField.swift block records the decision NOT to port the debounce. So the row anatomy at ComplexModificationsView.swift:125-254 is a NEW port and needs its own nine-field block in this PR, and the debounced search is not available as transferable here — if this bead wants a debounce it must justify it in CrossOS's own words and must not cite SearchField.swift for it.

**rectangle is the other half, and its grade is NO.** `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md:1231` grades it inside the "Everything (... rectangle ...)" row: concepts, behavior and UX only, reimplement through CrossOS contracts, no code. Both rectangle references get that verdict and neither is a copy target, so no rectangle file may be cited as a source of code. The two ideas are a recorder that suspends live bindings while it records, and a validator that refuses a combo another binding already holds. `third_party/rectangle/ATTRIBUTION.md` carries only `Rectangle/PrefsWindow/SnapAreaViewController.swift` today, so each new idea needs its own nine-field block. Cite each as "idea, no vendored file" unless you can point at a file you actually resolved, because an unverifiable `file:line` citation is worse than none: the next agent cannot tell a drifted line number from a wrong repository. In particular do NOT reach for a `PassthroughShortcutValidator` as the model for the refusal half — that class's `isShortcutAlreadyTaken` returns false, so it never refuses a taken combo, and pointing an implementer at it sends them to copy the one class whose entire purpose is to disable the refusal.

**Both references need their own nine-field blocks, and this bead APPENDS only.** Two things this bead does NOT do, both owned elsewhere. It does not repair block 1 of `third_party/rectangle/ATTRIBUTION.md` — block 1 is missing `Source file:` and `Reason for modification:`, and that repair is cross-os-baz's, whose acceptance criterion says so; this bead must not re-add either line, and after baz lands the file is already well-formed and this bead only appends. It does not decide the repository name: the plan names `rxhanson/rectangle` at `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md:1133` and `:1291` while the repository is `ramonwessels/rectangle` (`third_party/rectangle/ATTRIBUTION.md:3`), the pin `12a9bc79f99abeb86297da3d7436b4489f920fa2` cannot be verified against a name that does not resolve, and cross-os-xxr owns that correction. This bead is BLOCKED on both: do not start until cross-os-baz and cross-os-xxr are closed, and do not guess either value.

Two safety claims about the gate are true TODAY and stop being true when baz lands, recorded so the implementer writes every field rather than relying on invisibility: `scripts/ci/license-gate.sh:97` counts `Source file:` entries against VENDORED source files and no rectangle source is vendored, so the count is satisfied by the blocks alone; and the nine-field loop at `license-gate.sh:144-149` runs once per FILE rather than once per BLOCK. cross-os-baz changes the second half, and baz is unblocked by anything here. If baz has already merged when this bead runs, the blocks written here are CI-enforced and a missing field is a red rather than a human-review duty. Either way, write all nine fields in every block.

Declare all three kinds in one change. Declaring two strands the conflicts bridge on a surface no page reaches, and the slice that reports a collision BEFORE it fires would have nothing to render.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] cross-os-baz and cross-os-xxr are CLOSED before this change starts, and the PR says which order they landed in. Both are preconditions this bead cannot satisfy itself: baz owns the repair of `third_party/rectangle/ATTRIBUTION.md` block 1, and xxr owns the corrected repository name for rectangle (the plan names `rxhanson/rectangle` at `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md:1133` and `:1291`; the repository is `ramonwessels/rectangle`, `third_party/rectangle/ATTRIBUTION.md:3`, and the pin `12a9bc79f99abeb86297da3d7436b4489f920fa2` cannot be verified against a name that does not resolve). A guessed repository name is how an unverifiable citation gets written. The dependency edges already enforce the order; a bead whose declared dependency is unmet stays open and blocked, and this one is exactly that.
- [ ] This bead APPENDS to `third_party/rectangle/ATTRIBUTION.md` only. Its block 1 already carries its `Source file:` and `Reason for modification:` lines (baz repaired them), and this change adds exactly the two new blocks named in the design. It must not re-add either line to block 1.
- [ ] core.keyboard declares ruleBuilder, keymapEditor and conflictResolver. All three are already keys in RENDERERS (app/frontend/src/controls/index.tsx:78, :83, :94), so this trips no coverage gate and adds no obligation to the every-registered-kind sweep at renderers.test.tsx:422-454.
- [ ] ConflictResolver STOPS deriving collisions from `Traces()`. The current derivation (`app/frontend/src/controls/ConflictResolver.tsx:56`) only surfaces a chord the user has ALREADY pressed, and only within the recorded-decision tail, so leaving it in place and ADDING the conflicts list renders both the real pre-flight warning and a stale post-hoc one on the same screen, which is worse than either. The `core:conflicts` source replaces the derivation; `Traces()` stays the Observe page's source and is not read here.
- [ ] Service.Conflicts returns the daemon's router-derived verdict — for every chord two still-firing rules claim, winner, sorted loser rule ids, and each claimant's plugin and human action name, computed by compiling the candidate group into a real `event.Router` and calling `Decide` in each declared app context (`core/cmd/crossos/pagedata.go:1431-1468`; the compile/Decide loop at :1440-1446, the claimant rows at :1458-1465, `sort.Strings(row.Losers)` at :1466). ConflictResolver renders one row per contested chord. **The Turn off button is per loser, and what it may write depends on which table the loser came from.** A loser whose `plugin` is `userrules.PluginID` (`"user"`, core/pkg/userrules/userrules.go:42) is a USER RULE and is NOT switchable: `config.setRuleEnabled` validates against `builtin.All()` only (`c.knownRuleIDs`, core/cmd/crossos/main.go:321-328) and fails closed in the store with `settings: unknown rule "<id>"` (core/pkg/settings/settings.go:378-381), and `userrules.Rule` carries no `Enabled` field. For a user-rule loser the control MUST say in words that the only way to stop it firing is to remove it, naming `config.deleteUserRule`, and MUST NOT render a Turn off button that is known to be refused — `handleConflicts` deliberately admits user-authored rules (pagedata.go:1052-1059), so these rows are common, not exotic. A builtin loser keeps the button and writes through SetRuleEnabled as before.
- [ ] A chord contested by two rules is reported BEFORE the user presses it. The assertion is that `core:conflicts` is reachable while the recorded-decision list is empty — the current shape can only ever see a chord already pressed, which is the whole defect.
- [ ] THREE existing vitest fixtures are rewritten in the same change, or the suite goes red: `the conflict resolver` at `app/frontend/src/controls/remap.test.tsx:526-570` feeds `daemon({Traces: ...})` in all three cases and will stop reaching the control; and the e2e `stub` fixture (`app/frontend/src/test/fixtures.ts:650-827`) gains `Conflicts`, because `app/frontend/src/e2e/firstRun.test.tsx:251-255` asserts the Conflicts pane reads "won by user.2" off the rows and the resolver would otherwise take its failure path and go blank. Both land with the source switch, in the same change.
- [ ] Service.Conflicts and Service.UserRuleVocabulary are added to the frozen list in `TestServiceExposesFrozenSources` (app/backend/uisources_test.go:457-476); its loop at :488-492 fails any bound method absent from that list, under ci.yml:42.
- [ ] Service.UserRuleVocabulary feeds the rule builder's pickers, and the split is decided in the PR rather than assumed. `app_modes` MUST be offered from the served `app_modes` list and a picked mode must reach the write — `blankRule()`'s hard-coded `app_modes: []` (app/frontend/src/controls/RuleBuilderControl.tsx:67) is the placeholder this removes. `device_id` is the opposite case and MUST NOT be given a picker: the daemon serves no device list (`getUserRuleVocabulary` returns app_modes, app_categories, modifiers, keys, capabilities, actions — core/cmd/crossos/userules.go:151-161; core/pkg/userrules/vocabulary.go exposes no device source), and `device_id: ""` is not a stub — `derive` reads an empty DeviceID as the legitimate "claims no device" value and raises the rule's scope to Global or App (core/pkg/userrules/userrules.go:132-142). The builder therefore either keeps emitting `""` deliberately, with a comment citing derive, or drops the field from the editable dimensions and says so. It MUST NOT synthesize a device vocabulary the validator does not hold, because a picker whose options disagree with the validator produces a selection the daemon refuses.
- [ ] The new row anatomy gets its own nine-field block in `third_party/Karabiner-Elements/ATTRIBUTION.md`, pinned to the commit that file already carries. The existing ComplexModificationsView.swift block records only the keyword-filter rule and the SearchField.swift block records the decision NOT to port the debounce, so neither covers this port. All nine fields.
- [ ] Window chords in the Windows page are recorded, not typed. This is a control on a DIFFERENT page (`core.windows`, group shortcuts Order 30) from the one this bead edits, and `ChordRecorder` already exists and is already used by KeymapEditorControl and RuleBuilderControl — wire it per row on `ShortcutListControl`'s `shortcutList` (source `core:windowShortcuts`).
- [ ] Any `core.`-prefixed ACTION id this change introduces is ASSEMBLED, never written out — `['core', 'conflicts'].join('.')`, the convention at app/frontend/src/controls/actions.ts:41 and :58. A literal fails `the shell source > names no page, control or plugin id anywhere in src` (app/frontend/src/test/shell.test.tsx:152-169), which walks every .ts/.tsx/.css under `src` for the needle `['core','.'].join('')` and expects zero hits; there are zero occurrences of `core.` anywhere under `app/frontend/src` today. SOURCE names use a colon (`core:keymapEditor`, `core:conflicts`, `core:windowShortcuts`) and are unaffected. The design section states this; it is restated here so the rule survives an edit to the prose.
- [ ] `cd app && go vet ./... && go test -short ./...` and `cd app/frontend && npm install && npm test` are green. The first IS enforced (ci.yml:42); the second runs nowhere but your machine — see the reviewer note on cross-os-vrx. Run the first on a clean checkout or after `cd app && wails3 generate bindings ./`: a stale local app/frontend/bindings/ makes `TestBindingsShimParity` red for methods added since your last generation, and that red is not this bead.

title: Install the launchd agent so the daemon survives reboot
description:
Audit blocker: scripts/launchd/dev.crossos.daemon.plist exists only as a repository file. Nothing copies it to ~/Library/LaunchAgents, so RunAtLoad never fires on a real install. A user who installs the app, reboots and opens it gets a window dialing a socket nobody is serving.

Pass criteria:
- A documented, non-interactive way to install the agent (subcommand or install script) that copies the plist, rewrites the binary path to the installed daemon, and bootstraps it
- A matching uninstall that stops and removes the agent (Reset Everything's 'remove login item' step needs this to be true rather than aspirational)
- Installing twice is safe and reports what it did
- The plist's ProgramArguments stops being a placeholder the user must edit by hand
- Wired into the onboarding/run path so the choice is visible, not folklore

title: P0 Safety contract (core/pkg/safety): ownership rollback, TRIAL, kill switch, Reset
description:
Parent: cross-os-ymh



## Background

P0 contract (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md Section 3.10, Section 8). Safety model: ownership rollback, IntegrationState (NOT a system snapshot), TRIAL trial-state, explicit-approve permissions (no auto-approve, not even safe defaults), kill switch (PANIC STOP), Reset Everything.



## Reasoning

CrossOS intercepts input system-wide. A bad rule or plugin must be reversible in one click and never strand OS state. The rollback boundary must be explicit now: CrossOS rolls back CrossOS-owned state only, never arbitrary OS state (Accessibility grants, foreign login items).



## Scope

- IntegrationState + IntegrationRecord types (plugin ID, type, identifier, state-before, rollback func)

- Ownership tracking on every system modification (creator plugin ID, timestamp, rollback procedure)

- TRIAL transactional enable: DISABLED to TRIAL to ENABLED; crash/timeout/kill-switch during TRIAL to DISABLED; 30s safe-mode confirm/rollback

- Kill switch: disable interception + plugin actions + flush/close (login item stays)

- Reset Everything: remove login item, disable extension, clean CrossOS-owned state, verify no process remains

- Explicit-approve permission prompts with least-privilege manifest check (over-scoped manifests rejected)



## Pass criteria

- [ ] Safety package with IntegrationState, ownership records, TRIAL flow, kill switch, reset

- [ ] No auto-approve path anywhere (test: enabling without user confirm stays un-enabled)

- [ ] Rollback removes/restores only CrossOS-owned resources (documented boundary)



## Plan refs

COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md: Section 3.10 Lifecycle and Safety, Section 8 Safety and Reversibility, Section 3.7 Permission Manager.

- [ ] Unit + e2e green: TRIAL enable flow, kill switch, Reset Everything, ownership rollback; every safety transition logged with plugin ID + timestamp
- [ ] TRIAL timeout (30s per Section 8.1) defined ONCE as a named Core constant; UI beads (ymh.3, nir.4, jpr.1) reference it, never a second hardcoded value
close_reason: Implemented + reviewed: core/pkg/safety (TRIAL flow, 30s timeout, kill switch, reset, scope check, audit). 8 tests green; vet/build/fmt clean.

title: Wire live tap into daemon: install + run loop + live decision path
description:
Blocker: core/internal/adapter tap bridge is a dead library — the daemon never imports it, never calls TapInstall (grep NewKeyboardTap in cmd/ + pkg/ = 0 hits). Two compounding defects:

1. NO INSTALL: cmd/crossos/main.go never imports core/internal/adapter, so nothing calls TapInstall. Even with TCC consent the running app intercepts nothing.
2. NO RUN LOOP: cxtap_create does CFRunLoopAddSource(CFRunLoopGetCurrent(), ...), but the daemon main blocks on a signal channel — no thread ever runs that CFRunLoop, so even an installed tap never fires callbacks.
3. STALE BINDING: crossosGoDecide calls decideExport.Decide, a fixed func set at Driver construction. The daemon's live decision path is decideLocked (respects plugin enable + rule toggles from config.json). The tap must route to decideLocked, not a snapshot.

Pass criteria:
- Daemon installs the tap at startup on a dedicated locked OS thread and runs its CFRunLoop (source actually delivers callbacks)
- Tap denial is non-fatal: daemon still serves IPC, status reports interception off
- Tap decision routes through the daemon's live decideLocked path (config.setRuleEnabled toggles take effect on the live tap, not a stale snapshot)
- Uninstall/stop is clean (no goroutine leak, tap disabled on SIGTERM)
- core.keyEvent diagnostic + IPC surface unchanged

No Xcode/secrets needed. Tier-2 (TCC consent) stays manual on a consented machine.

title: Spike D Finder Sync (extensions/finder-sync): menu via Unix socket, daemon-down hide
description:
Parent: cross-os-ymh

## Background
Phase 0 Spike D proves the Finder Sync platform extension path (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md Phase 0 checklist, Section 6.3): FIFinderSync menu to Unix socket IPC to Core daemon, with daemon-down graceful fallback.

## Reasoning
Finder Sync extensions run in Finder process space. A blocking or crashing extension degrades Finder itself. The extension must be a minimal IPC client that hides (never blocks) when the daemon is down.

## Scope
Minimal FIFinderSync extension: builds one menu item, sends request over Unix socket to a stub daemon; daemon-down path hides the menu without blocking Finder.

## Pass criteria
- [ ] Menu item appears in Finder context menu
- [ ] Menu action reaches stub daemon over Unix socket IPC
- [ ] Daemon-down: extension hides/fails gracefully, Finder never blocks
- [ ] Note: extension sends requests only, never executable code (Section 3.7 security model)

## Plan refs
COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md: Phase 0 Spike D, Section 6.3, Section 3.7 Permission Manager, Section 9.11 newfile COPY/ADAPT source.

description:
Parent: cross-os-ymh

## Background
P0 contract, must be reviewed before any plugin code (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md Section 3.6, Section 3.6c, Phase 0 checklist). Locks the Plugin API v1 surface: plugins REGISTER behavior, Core owns the pipeline; no per-event fast-path callbacks.

## Reasoning
Go .so via plugin.Open() is explicitly REJECTED (OS/version/symbol fragility). MVP 0 ships builtin + declarative only; Level B executable is MVP 1. Locking this contract prevents plugin code from depending on unstable internals.

## Scope
- Manifest schema: ID, name, version, entry, type (builtin/declarative/executable/extpack), permissions, capabilities, config_schema, hooks, safety
- Lifecycle: DISABLED to TRIAL to ENABLED with rollback (Section 3.10)
- Decision enum (canonical, ONLY vocabulary): PASS / CONSUME / REPLACE with DecisionReplace normative note (suppress original + execute Intent; does NOT imply synthetic injection)
- apiVersion: independent manifestVersion / pluginApiVersion / capabilityApiVersion + minCoreVersion
- RegisterUI + UIContribution schema (Section 3.6c): namespaced IDs, declarative settings-page/section/sidebar MVP tier; custom-view REJECTED for MVP
- Hook semantics: onIntent/onEvent/onContext are async slow-path observers, never decision hooks
- Capability ownership: core IDs reserved, RegisterCapability rejects plugin shadowing

## Pass criteria
- [ ] pluginapi package (or proto/JSON schema) with Manifest, Registry, Decision, Capability, UIContribution, Hook types
- [ ] Ownership rule enforced in RegisterCapability (test: plugin claiming window.close fails)
- [ ] Contract reviewed + approved before any plugin code lands
- [ ] apiVersion fields present and checked at load

COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md: Section 3.6 Plugin Runtime, Section 3.6c UI Contribution API, Section 3.10 Lifecycle, Section 3.12 registry.

title: CI: run the frontend suite, so the vitest gates are not developer-only
description:
No workflow in `.github/workflows` runs node, npm or vitest — all three files (ci.yml, license-gate.yml, release.yml) were grepped and none matches. ci.yml is gofmt, `go vet` + `go test -short` over core/app/platform/extensions, the build matrix, the windows-dll job, finder-appex and license-gate; license-gate.yml is bash. `scripts/dev-verify.sh:172-190` runs only `npx tsc --noEmit` and returns early with a warning (not a failure) when `app/frontend/node_modules` (:175-178) or the generated Wails bindings (:179-182) are absent.

Consequence: every frontend regression in the current audit slice reached main because no job runs `npm test` — the unregistered `menuList` renderer, the unbound `core.setMenuItemEnabled`, the dead Open System Settings button. All eight beads under review carry acceptance criteria that only that suite can check. The `core.` shell-source gate (`app/frontend/src/test/shell.test.tsx:152-169`) and the kind-coverage gate (`renderers.test.tsx:301-314`) are advisory today.

**This bead is NOT the repository's only red CI leg, and the distinction is why it is P1 rather than P0.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:40` already runs `cd core && go vet ./... && go test -short ./...` on the `macos-latest, windows-latest` matrix (the os list is the single line ci.yml:26; the same step serves both legs), and on windows-latest that command fails 8 tests today: six `absoluteSlash` path assertions, one hardcoded `/tmp/crossos-test/` prefix, one Windows rename sharing violation. That red is cross-os-qji's, is not in this bead's scope, and is recorded here so no reader takes "main is green except the frontend" away from this bead. A missing frontend lane is a miss of PREVENTION; a red required job is a live defect, and the live defect gets the P0.

The one hazard this bead must not rediscover — gitignored Wails bindings, TS2307, which criteria depend on the typecheck, and the `dev-verify.sh` skip — is stated in full in the design, and belongs there rather than here.
design:
The job, the `scripts/dev-verify.sh` decision, and the first-run result. NOT in scope: fixing whatever the first run surfaces — those become their own beads, so this one is closeable on its own.

**Shape.** One required `frontend` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, on the same `macos-latest, windows-latest` matrix the Go lanes use (the os list is the single line ci.yml:26). It runs `npm ci`, then `npm test`, then — only if the bindings were generated — `npx tsc --noEmit`. Nothing else: the job installs node and runs the suite; it does not grow into a lint job or a build job.

**The hazard this bead exists partly to not rediscover.** `app/frontend/bindings/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:34`; `git ls-files app/frontend/bindings` returns zero files) and `app/frontend/src/lib/service.ts:19` imports `../../bindings/crossos/app/backend` under a tsconfig whose `include` is `["src", "bindings"]` with `allowJs: true`. So `tsc --noEmit` emits TS2307 on a clean checkout. `npm test` alone is safe without the bindings — `app/frontend/src/test/harness.tsx:48` mocks that import — which is exactly why the test half looks fine and the typecheck half is the trap. `scripts/dev-verify.sh:179-181` already refuses to run that same command for the same reason and is the model to follow. The job either runs `cd app && wails3 generate bindings ./` first (the form `scripts/dev-verify.sh:129` uses) or drops the typecheck and says so in the PR. A typecheck that cannot resolve its imports checks nothing while reporting green.

**What the typecheck is carrying.** The `ServiceApi` and `controlSurface` criteria in cross-os-s0s, cross-os-b6s, cross-os-1uu, cross-os-pbd and cross-os-n4n are enforced by that run and by nothing else. This job is therefore not only about the frontend's own tests.

**The skip decision is in scope, and its default is to stop reporting "cannot check" as a pass.** `scripts/dev-verify.sh:172-190` runs only `npx tsc --noEmit` and returns early with a `warn` and `return 0` when node_modules (:175-178) or the generated bindings (:179-182) are absent. Either the script stops skipping, or the skip is explicitly scoped to an interactive dev convenience and labelled as one. Leaving it as a silent green is what lets a broken typecheck read as a checked one.

**Ordering, and why the first run's output is a deliverable.** The job lands after cross-os-vrx — that edge is why vrx's own first run executes the two vitest gates this job installs (`renderers.test.tsx:301-314` and `:211-215`) before this job exists to report them. Whatever else the first run surfaces becomes its own bead rather than being fixed here, and the first run's output is quoted in the PR either way.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A required `frontend` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `npm ci && npm test` on macos-latest and windows-latest, and runs `tsc --noEmit` on the same matrix ONLY after the Wails bindings are generated. `npm ci && npm test` needs nothing generated — `app/frontend/src/test/harness.tsx:48` does `vi.mock('../lib/service', ...)`, which is why the test half passes on a clean checkout and the gap is easy to miss. The typecheck does need them.
- [ ] The job generates the Wails bindings before typechecking, or the typecheck is dropped with that reason recorded in the PR. `app/frontend/bindings/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:34`; `git ls-files app/frontend/bindings` returns zero files) and `app/frontend/src/lib/service.ts:19` imports `../../bindings/crossos/app/backend` under a tsconfig whose `include` is `["src", "bindings"]` with `allowJs: true`, so `tsc --noEmit` emits TS2307 on a clean checkout — a typecheck that cannot resolve its imports checks nothing while reporting green. `scripts/dev-verify.sh:179-181` already refuses to run that exact command unless `app/frontend/bindings/crossos/app/backend/service.js` exists, and is the model. Run `cd app && wails3 generate bindings ./` in the job (the form `scripts/dev-verify.sh:129` and `docs/dev-verification.md` use), or state in the PR that the typecheck is deferred and why. This is not a nicety: the `ServiceApi` and `controlSurface` criteria in cross-os-s0s, cross-os-b6s, cross-os-1uu, cross-os-pbd and cross-os-n4n are checked by that run and by nothing else. The design states this hazard in full; it is restated here so the checklist can be read on its own.
- [ ] scripts/dev-verify.sh no longer silently skips the frontend suite when node_modules or the generated bindings are absent, or that skip is explicitly scoped to an interactive dev convenience and labelled as such. Today both are `warn` + `return 0` (:175-178, :179-182) — "cannot check" is reported as a pass.
- [ ] The result of the FIRST run on the current tree is recorded in the PR. This job is ordered after cross-os-vrx by dependency, and the order matters: vrx's first run is what executes the two vitest gates this job installs — `renderers.test.tsx:301-314` (kind coverage, red on `menuList`) and `renderers.test.tsx:211-215` (action coverage, red on `core.setMenuItemEnabled`). Landing this job first would carve a second P0 out of a P1 by turning two known, already-scoped fixes into "those failures become their own beads". If the first run is red for other reasons, those become their own beads rather than being fixed inside this one.

title: Audit wave: red gates, dead seams, and the Product UI screen plan
description:
The audit wave that found the Product UI's real state, in one place: the product cases and the gates underneath them, in the order they unblock each other.

**The finding this epic exists to record.** A Product UI audit of the tree (shell survey, Go data-surface survey, roadmap/bead survey, and reference-mining of the OSS repos already cloned under `third_party/` and `.tmp/research/`) concluded that the missing Product UI is not missing REACT — it is missing SEAMS. The control-kind registry renders server-declared controls; a page is a Go change with zero UI change. What is actually absent is (1) bridges from registered daemon verbs to the Wails Service, (2) control kinds that exist in the registry but that no Go page declares, and (3) the gates that would have caught both. Every bead below is one of those, not a redesign.

**Two load-bearing facts, both established by running the commands, not by reading them.**

1. `main` is RED on a required CI lane, not only in the frontend. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:40` runs `cd core && go vet ./... && go test -short ./...` on a `macos-latest, windows-latest` matrix (the os list is the single line ci.yml:26; the same step serves both legs) under a header at ci.yml:12 that says "No test exclusions". On a windows-latest checkout that command fails 8 tests across 2 packages: six through `absoluteSlash` (POSIX `path.IsAbs` refusing every `C:\...` path a Windows `t.TempDir()` produces), one hardcoded `/tmp/crossos-test/` prefix, one Windows rename sharing violation. That is cross-os-qji. No agent in this epic may start from the belief that the tree is otherwise green.

2. No workflow runs node, npm or vitest at all. `grep -rniE "npm|node|vitest" .github/workflows/` returns nothing across ci.yml, license-gate.yml and release.yml. The kind-coverage gate (`renderers.test.tsx:301-314`) and the action-binding gate (`:211-215`) are advisory only, which is how the unregistered `menuList` renderer, the unbound `core.setMenuItemEnabled` and the dead Open System Settings button all reached main. That is cross-os-64q.

**A convention that will bite every implementer in this epic.** `app/frontend/src/test/shell.test.tsx:152-169` greps every `.ts/.tsx/.css` file under `app/frontend/src` for the literal string `core.` and asserts zero hits — a page, control or plugin id must never appear in the shell's source. The repo's own convention is to assemble the token so the grep cannot see it: `app/frontend/src/controls/actions.ts:41` writes `['core', 'setObserve'].join('.')`, never the literal, and the same file assembles the file-type pair at `:48-49` and the switcher pair at `:58-59`. Several beads in this epic ask an implementer to BIND a new action id. Writing the id literally, in a hurry, in the one file that binds actions, turns a green gate red and looks like a product regression.

**Order.** The three P0s are independent of one another and can run in parallel: cross-os-qji (the red required lane), cross-os-vrx (Explorer page broken on every build), cross-os-tsd (the wizard never stops leading, and never stops leading on relaunch either). Everything in the P1/P2 set sequences off one of those or off a P1 of its own: cross-os-64q and cross-os-tcd off vrx; cross-os-s0s off tsd; cross-os-b6s off vrx AND qji; cross-os-n4n off qji; cross-os-pbd off qji; cross-os-1uu off baz and xxr. cross-os-s6e is a ROOT of its own chain: cross-os-baz and cross-os-xxr both depend on it and it depends on nothing here. `br dep cycles` is empty (bvr reports `has_cycles: false`) and `bvr --robot-triage` ranks cross-os-vrx, cross-os-s6e, cross-os-qji, cross-os-tsd first — the three P0s interleaved with the P1 that unblocks two beads.

**The macos leg was not run.** The beads that touch CI state say so rather than asserting it. Do not upgrade any such claim without running it.

- Canonical registry v1 with permission + platform + reversibility per capability

- [ ] Naming-convention lock documented: permission vs capability vs intent; invalid names (keyboard.intercept, window.manage) rejected

title: Explorer: bridge the five daemon verbs the page already declares
description:
The daemon side of the Explorer page is rich and complete; the shell has none of it. This is the largest single unbridged surface in the tree.

The daemon serves all seven menu items in table order — never a shorter list, so a disabled item is a row the user can switch back on — each with its id, title, contexts (file/folder/empty), `needsPaths`, capability, the user's toggle, and a `Supported` verdict that distinguishes "capability not in the intent registry" from "adapter present but the platform refuses it" (`core/cmd/crossos/finderdata.go:79-87`). **The menu VERB is not on the row**: `findermenu.Item` (`core/pkg/findermenu/menu.go:44-51`) carries exactly six fields — ID, Title, Contexts, NeedsPaths, Capability, Enabled — and the verb names (`finder.copyPath`, `finder.duplicateWithName`, ...) exist only as string keys in the separate appex-side `finderMenuHandlers` map (`core/cmd/crossos/findermenu.go:39-50`), never on the wire. `core.fileTypes` serves the 8 seeded presets with a derived `MenuTitle` and a stored order. `core.setFileType` is a validated read-modify-write of one existing row; `core.reorderFileTypes` requires a COMPLETE permutation and refuses duplicates, omissions and inventions. All five verbs are registered at `core/cmd/crossos/main.go:866-870`.

`app/backend/service.go` has NONE of the five corresponding methods, so `FinderMenuControl` and `FileTypeListControl` both Partial-probe for them and render empty or refusing states on every build. The served Explorer page draws "This build has no binding for the file-type catalog".

Three persistence defects sit behind the binding and are part of doing this properly:

1. **The menu toggle is IN-MEMORY ONLY.** `core.setMenuItemEnabled` mutates `c.menuOff` (declared `main.go:78`, mutated at `core/cmd/crossos/finderdata.go:143-145`) and never writes to `c.set`; `settings.Store` has no `menuOff` field and the document has no key for it (`settings.go:115-125`). A restart re-enables every item the user switched off. The file-type catalog, by contrast, does persist (`document.FileTypes`, `settings.go:124`). Both readers are Go, so the regression test goes in `core/cmd/crossos`, not vitest.

2. **Two readers of one catalog disagree.** `finder.menuEntries` — the menu the appex actually renders — serves `filetype.Seeds()` (`findermenu.go:70-80`), NOT the store's edited catalog that `core.fileTypes`/`core.setFileType` write through. A file type the user disabled in the UI still appears in the real Finder menu, and a `displayName` edit never reaches it. This is the exact bug shape `.tmp/research/newfile/CLAUDE.md:48` records as its own roadmap issue #2 (`third_party/newfile/` holds only ATTRIBUTION.md, LICENSE and NOTICE — there is no CLAUDE.md anywhere under `third_party/`, and citing one would also put a dev-notes file into the one directory `license-gate.sh` measures as vendored source).

3. **`clipboard.copyRelativePath` and `duplicateWithName` are greyed on every host** (`finderdata.go:64-69`) because the intent registry has not gained them — I confirmed neither appears in `core/pkg/intent/registry_v1.go` — even though both verbs have working handlers. Note the mismatch: the menu ITEM is `duplicateWithName`, the CAPABILITY is `filesystem.duplicate`, and the registry carries only `clipboard.copyPath`. The page must show the daemon's reason in words, not a mystery disabled row.
design:
NINE edits, not four, and the build breaks on every one you skip:

title: License gate: assert the nine mandatory fields per BLOCK, not per file
description:
`scripts/ci/license-gate.sh` is the only automated enforcement of §9.11's nine-field ATTRIBUTION format, and it is blind in two ways that together make a missing block invisible.

1. **The count check compares against VENDORED files.** `license-gate.sh:96-111` counts `Source file:` entries (`nentries` at :97) and compares them to `nfiles`/`fsfiles`, the source files under `third_party/<repo>/` (:98, :102, :103; the comparison is at :108-111). I audited all eight directories: third_party vendors ZERO source files in every one of them (`find third_party -name '*.swift'` also returns zero), so the count is trivially satisfied by the blocks alone. An entirely unattributed new structural port cannot turn the gate red — which is exactly what cross-os-b6s, cross-os-1uu and cross-os-n4n are each about to add.

2. **The completeness check is per FILE, not per BLOCK.** `license-gate.sh:147` runs `grep -q "^$field" "$dir/ATTRIBUTION.md"` inside a `for field` loop, asserting each of the nine fields appears at least once in the whole file. I verified the consequence by auditing every block of every directory: `third_party/rectangle/ATTRIBUTION.md` has THREE blocks but only TWO `Source file:` lines and TWO `Reason for modification:` lines — block 1 is missing both outright, with `SettingsViewController.swift:307-311`, `:10,15` and `:60` named only inside the `Modification:` prose — and the gate reports `PASS [rectangle]`. That block is the ONLY incomplete block in the tree; the other seven directories and rectangle's other two blocks all carry all nine fields.

The single highest-leverage correction is to make the gate assert nine fields per BLOCK. That one change converts a whole class of omission from invisible to CI-red, and it is cheap.
design: The two failure modes are different and the second is the cheap one. The per-BLOCK completeness assertion is a small change to the existing field loop and is worth doing regardless. The per-BLOCK-to-vendored-file mapping is NOT solvable mechanically — `license-gate.sh`'s own header already concedes that correctness-of-mapping is a human duty, and that concession should stay. The deliverable is the completeness assertion plus an honest header, not an attempt to auto-verify mapping.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] cross-os-s6e is closed FIRST, so `bash scripts/ci/license-gate.sh --all` is green before this bead changes the script. Today that command fails on exactly one directory — run on this tree it prints `license-gate FAIL [alt-tab-macos]: missing third_party/alt-tab-macos/LICENSE` and `license-gate: FAIL`, with the other seven passing — so no "all eight pass" claim in this PR is honest until s6e lands. Do NOT edit the gate to work around it: the GPL ban (`DECL_BANNED` at `scripts/ci/license-gate.sh:66`, applied to `Original license:` at `:126`) and the LICENSE+NOTICE+ATTICE+ATTRIBUTION requirement (`:78-83`) are correct behaviour, and the directory is what is wrong.
- [ ] The PR quotes the output of `bash scripts/ci/license-gate.sh --all` after the change, showing all eight directories passing with the per-BLOCK check on. `--all` is the only mode that demonstrates this bead's work: the CI job runs `--diff origin/main` (ci.yml:161), which is EMPTY for anything already merged and would stay green through a per-BLOCK check that never fires.
- [ ] license-gate.sh parses each third_party/*/ATTRIBUTION.md into blocks at each `^Source repository:` line and asserts all nine mandatory fields per BLOCK, naming the block's repository and commit on failure.
- [ ] third_party/rectangle/ATTRIBUTION.md block 1 is repaired in this PR — it is missing `Source file:` and `Reason for modification:` (3 blocks, 2 `Source file:`, 2 `Reason for modification:`; the `SettingsViewController.swift` file:lines appear only inside the `Modification:` prose), so the tightened gate does not land red. Audited block by block across all eight directories, this is the ONLY incomplete block in the tree, which is why the repair is this bead's and not a neighbour's. **Both land in ONE commit, in this order: the repair first, the tightened loop second** — a per-BLOCK check that lands first is an immediate CI red. This repair is BAZ'S; cross-os-1uu depends on this bead and must not also do it, so by the time 1uu runs the file is already well-formed and 1uu only appends.
- [ ] A scratch fixture with one well-formed block and one block missing `Source file:` FAILS the gate, proving the new check fires. The self-test at `scripts/ci/test-license-gate.sh` is the right home; it already runs in the license-gate job before the real gate.
- [ ] The gate header comment states what the gate still cannot verify — the entry-to-file mapping is a human-reviewer duty — so the improved check is not mistaken for full coverage. The per-BLOCK-to-vendored-file mapping is not mechanically solvable and that concession stays.

title: Tap decision path uses the focused app, not a hardcoded empty AppID
description:
Found by TestMacKeycodesDriveRules while landing cross-os-uok.

crossosGoDecide builds the decision context as event.FastContext{AppMode: AppModeNative} — AppID is always empty. Every app-scoped rule is therefore unreachable from the LIVE tap: the developer plugin's Ctrl+Shift+C/P (scoped to VSCode/Cursor/Terminal...) can never match, because the router compares ctx.AppID against the rule's AppIDs list. Only the two globally-scoped rules (windows-keyboard, launcher) work.

The tap also never sees the focused app because nothing consults the AX bridge. Per-keystroke AX queries would blow the <1ms fast-path budget (spike A/C), so the context must be CACHED and refreshed off the hot path.

Pass criteria:
- The tap decision path resolves the focused app from a CACHED snapshot, not a per-key query
- The cache refreshes on app change (AX observer or a bounded-interval refresh off the callback thread) and is documented as such
- A Driver-level seam supplies the context; nil falls back to AppModeNative with an empty AppID (current behaviour, honestly named)
- No AX call happens inside the CGEventTap callback
- Tests: an app-scoped rule matches through the real tap path when the cache says the app is focused, and misses when it is not

title: Profiles: a one-click Windows experience, and a way back
description:
Two of this bead's three original claims are already false. The profile concept EXISTS: `core/pkg/profiles/profiles.go` ships the bundle (id `windows-11-experience`, label "Windows 11 Experience", five capabilities — `profiles.go:98-148`). The page EXISTS: `app/backend/profilespage.go:19-26` registers `core.profiles` (nav group home, order 10) with a `profileList` control over `core:profiles` and `applyAction core:profileApply`.

But the profile is NOT picked from inside the wizard today, and an earlier draft of this bead said it was. `OnboardingFlow` (`app/backend/onboarding.go:29`) declares plain-string steps — `"steps": []string{"Welcome", "Enable per plugin", "Open System Settings", "Verify ready"}` — with no step object and no `body` key, and no Go page declares a `body` at all. The `chooseProfile` / `body: 'profileList'` step exists only in the e2e fixture (`app/frontend/src/test/fixtures.ts:105`). In-product profile selection is a fourth piece of scope, not a description of what ships.

Apply is real and atomic: `core/cmd/crossos/pagedata.go:908-950` projects the bundle into ONE `settings.Plan` and calls `Store.ApplyBatch` (`core/pkg/settings/settings.go:561`), which validates the whole plan before it writes.

**The revert is genuinely absent, and it is the whole remaining scope.** `planForProfile` (`pagedata.go:970-991`) only ever emits `settings.Toggle{Enabled:true}` — there is no disable path, no prior-state snapshot, no `core.profileDeactivate`, and `SetActiveProfile` is never called with `""`. A user who applies the Windows profile cannot return to a neutral state from the UI. `app/backend/profilespage.go:5-6` claims "turning it on is one choice instead of a row of toggles, and undoing it is one choice back" — no such choice exists in code, and the same page RENDERS a user-visible note at `:26` saying individual switches stay on Keyboard, Windows and Explorer. Both sentences contradict the code.

Also in scope, because the same control renders them: no preview (the Plan is computed server-side then discarded except for two integer counts, so "what would this change" is never shown before the click) and no per-capability switch (the rollup is a rollup, not a control — though note that profilespage.go:10-12 and ProfileListControl.tsx:17 currently state the opposite, so that boundary is part of the change).

And one stale fact to correct: `window.alt-tab` is declared unavailable at `profiles.go:136` although the switcher ships.
design:
Daemon: snapshot the prior state of every id the plan touches, then a `core.profileDeactivate` that restores it. The Plan already carries every toggle that would be written — the snapshot is the missing half, not a new model — but this bead fixes four things the earlier draft left open.

1. **A store-only revert is a half-revert.** `handleProfileApply` (`core/cmd/crossos/pagedata.go:918`) writes the store AND separately updates the running router's in-memory `c.plugins` map under `c.mu` (`:937-944`). The comment there names the exact failure: "The store persists; the RUNNING router reads c.plugins (decideLocked recompiles from it), so the plan's plugin verdicts are applied there too. A profile that saved to disk and left the daemon in its old state is the half-activated outcome ApplyBatch exists to prevent, one layer up." `core.profileDeactivate` MUST do both halves under the same lock, or the user clicks Revert, the disk agrees, the nav greys out, and the keyboard still runs the Windows profile until restart.

2. **The snapshot is PERSISTED, in the settings document, and written by the same `Store.ApplyBatch` call that applies the plan.** An in-memory snapshot is lost on restart, so Revert greys out forever for every user who quits between applying and undoing — a worse outcome than no Revert at all. The document's keys are enumerated at `core/pkg/settings/settings.go:115-125`; adding one means a default for a profile applied before the field existed, and the snapshot must ride the SAME atomic call as the apply (`ApplyBatch` validates then writes wholesale, `settings.go:561`) or a crash between them leaves a profile applied with nothing to undo.

3. **The snapshot covers rules, plugins AND the active-profile string.** `planForProfile` sets `settings.Plan{ActiveProfile: &id}` (`pagedata.go:972`), so the profile id is part of what the plan touched. Restoring the enablement without clearing it leaves the store claiming a profile is active that is not.

4. **Re-applying after a revert is covered.** The second apply must not restore the FIRST apply's snapshot as its undo point. The snapshot is overwritten by each apply, and a test covers apply -> revert -> apply -> revert.

UI: structural port, no code copied. The expand-in-place card with per-capability switches and the review-before-apply sheet are `.tmp/research/menumate/App/UI/PacksScreen.swift:255-368` (PackRow) and `.tmp/research/menumate/App/UI/PackImportSheet.swift:230-277` (reviewList). The sources live under `.tmp/research/`, NOT `third_party/`, which carries only ATTRIBUTION.md/LICENSE/NOTICE — `find third_party -name '*.swift'` returns zero, so every citation in this paragraph is resolved against the commit pinned in `third_party/menumate/ATTRIBUTION.md:4`.

One correction to the usual shorthand: menumate is §9.11 PARTIAL (`COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md:1228`) — "manifest/rule/config/IPC concepts + schema shapes may be ported; script executor is NOT copied". That is what is off-limits, NOT view files; the view files exist, which is why the two citations above are checkable. And PARTIAL is not a claim that no view-shaped reference has been recorded here: `third_party/menumate/ATTRIBUTION.md` already carries two App/UI structural-port blocks citing `App/UI/MenuHubScreen.swift` (the nav rail and the one-row-per-extension list). Neither of this bead's two files is named there, so both need their own nine-field block in this PR, pinned to the same 40-hex commit the file already carries, each stating `structural port, no code copied`. The viewed-all review gate and the "n of m enabled" rollup are the transferable ideas; the Swift source is not.

**Write all nine fields in both new blocks, and do not rely on the gate to tell you if you did not.** The gate would not notice an omission today: `scripts/ci/license-gate.sh:97` counts `Source file:` entries against VENDORED files, no menumate source is vendored, so the count is satisfied by the existing six blocks alone; and the nine-field loop at `license-gate.sh:144-149` runs once per FILE rather than once per BLOCK. cross-os-baz changes the second half, and baz is blocked by nothing in this slice — so these two blocks become CI-enforced the moment it lands. That is a reason to write all nine fields, not a reason to skip a block. It is NOT a reason for this bead to repair the six existing blocks: every block of `third_party/menumate/ATTRIBUTION.md` (6 blocks, at :3, :13, :23, :33, :43, :53) was audited and each carries all nine fields, so baz's tightened check passes on this file as it stands. If baz has already merged when this bead runs, re-run that audit rather than trusting this one.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] core.profileDeactivate (or UnapplyProfile) restores the exact prior enablement of every id the plan touched, the active-profile string, AND the running router's in-memory `c.plugins` map. The in-memory half is required: `handleProfileApply` updates it under `c.mu` (pagedata.go:937-944), so a store-only revert leaves the keyboard running the profile until restart — the half-activated outcome the existing comment there warns about. The test is that the daemon's decision path answers identically before apply and after revert, without a restart.
- [ ] The revert is a refusal, in words, when there is no snapshot to return to — never a button that greys out silently and never one that reports success.
- [ ] The snapshot is PERSISTED in the settings document and written by the same `Store.ApplyBatch` call that applies the plan. A profile applied before this change existed reverts to a stated behaviour, and that choice is recorded in the PR, not left to the implementer. A test covers apply -> revert -> apply -> revert.
- [ ] The profile card shows what applying will change BEFORE the click, not a count after it. The Plan is already computed server-side (pagedata.go:908-950) and discarded except for two integers, so the preview is a new served field, not a new control kind.
- [ ] A per-capability switch exists, AND the three statements that forbid it are changed in the SAME change, or the page contradicts itself: `app/backend/profilespage.go:10-12` (the boundary comment), `app/backend/profilespage.go:26` (the note the page RENDERS to the user — "Individual switches stay on Keyboard, Windows and Explorer"), and `app/frontend/src/controls/ProfileListControl.tsx:17`. Leaving the rendered note in place is the worst of the three: the user reads a sentence denying the switches they are looking at. The new boundary is stated in one place and the other two cite it.
- [ ] The new action id is ASSEMBLED, never a literal: `const PROFILE_DEACTIVATE = ['core', 'profileDeactivate'].join('.')`, the pattern at `app/frontend/src/controls/actions.ts:41-49`. The moment the id is declared on core.profiles it enters the declared-action set and `renderers.test.tsx:211-216` fails unless it is in ACTION_COMMANDS or UNBOUND_ACTIONS — the same commit. Written as a literal, `'core.profileDeactivate'` additionally fails `the shell source > names no page, control or plugin id anywhere in src` (app/frontend/src/test/shell.test.tsx:152-169), which walks every .ts/.tsx/.css under src for the needle `['core','.'].join('')` and expects zero hits.
- [ ] The new Service method is added to the frozen list in `TestServiceExposesFrozenSources` (app/backend/uisources_test.go:457-476); its loop at :488-492 fails any bound method absent from that list, under ci.yml:42.
- [ ] The Go-side snapshot and revert live in `core/cmd/crossos` with their test in the core module under `cd core && go test -short ./...` (ci.yml:40) — not in vitest, which cannot see the store.
- [ ] The window.alt-tab row stops telling a falsehood and tells the truth precisely. `window.switcher` IS in the intent registry (`core/pkg/intent/registry_v1.go:75`) and the switcher panel ships, so the current Reason at `profiles.go:136` — "no window-switcher capability, plugin, or rule exists yet" — is wrong about the capability. Do NOT flip Available to true: a registered capability is not a rule driving it, and `profiles.go:93-96` says a passing row must not advertise a control that does nothing. Rewrite the Reason to name only what is genuinely missing (the plugin and the rule that would drive window.switcher), and add a test asserting the Reason makes no claim the intent registry contradicts, so the next registry addition cannot leave the string stale again.
- [ ] `finder.explorer` (`profiles.go:142-145`) is re-checked in the same pass. Its Reason reads "F2 rename and Win+E have no rule or shortcut behind them; only the core file.moveToTrash capability exists, unclaimed". Either the capability now exists and Available flips, or the Reason is rewritten from the rule/capability tables rather than from memory. Leaving it is the same bug as the one this criterion fixes.

- [ ] REVIEWER NOTE: the two gates named above — `renderers.test.tsx:211-216` and `the shell source > names no page, control or plugin id anywhere in src` (`app/frontend/src/test/shell.test.tsx:152-169`) — are enforced by nothing today. No workflow in `.github/workflows` installs node, and `scripts/dev-verify.sh:172-190` runs only `npx tsc --noEmit`, skipping even that when node_modules (:175-178) or the generated Wails bindings (:179-182) are absent. A literal `core.profileDeactivate` is therefore a local mistake, not a red build, until cross-os-64q lands a frontend lane. Every Go criterion in this bead — the persisted snapshot, the router half of the revert, the `window.alt-tab` and `finder.explorer` Reason strings, and the frozen list — IS enforced, by ci.yml:40 and ci.yml:42. Quote in the PR which you ran; the full note is the reviewer note on cross-os-vrx.

# Extract nudge geometry primitives → window capability handlers

## Background
First Phase 2 task: port the window-geometry core from mikusnuz/nudge (MIT, direct-reuse YES per §9.11) into CrossOS contracts. Source files per §9.10 nudge row: `Nudge/Core/WindowManager.swift`, `Nudge/Core/SnapZone.swift`, `Nudge/Core/SnapAction.swift`, `Nudge/Helpers/AccessibilityHelper.swift`, `Nudge/Helpers/DisplayHelper.swift`, `Nudge/Core/DragSnapManager.swift`. # Level B executable-plugin runtime (out-of-process JSON-RPC)



## Background

Phase 2 introduces PluginType `executable` (Level B, Â§3.6): plugins run as child processes speaking JSON-RPC over stdio/Unix socket from `~/.crossos/plugins/<id>/{manifest.json, plugin}`. Core spawns the executable; a plugin crash never takes down Core (restart/disable). MVP 0 shipped builtin + declarative only (Â§3.6 layout note: "Level B is MVP 1"). This runtime is also the gate for shell execution in extension packs (Phase 3: shell is opt-in Level B only, Â§6.3).



## Reasoning

- Go `.so` via `plugin.Open()` explicitly REJECTED (Â§3.6) â€” out-of-process is the only sanctioned native-code extension mechanism.

- Fast-path invariant (Â§2 Data Flow): external Level B plugins are compiled into the cached matcher ahead of time and NEVER run synchronously in the native callback â€” a 100ms plugin hang would break typing.

- Health states feed the Plugins UI page (Â§7.2: local-only in MVP 1+, no marketplace until Phase 4) and Phase 4 lifecycle (DISABLED/TRIAL/HEALTHY/ENABLED).

- Capability ownership (Â§3.6): RegisterCapability rejects plugin claims on core-owned IDs â€” enforce in the loader.



## Pass criteria

- [ ] Core spawns Level B executables, speaks JSON-RPC over stdio + Unix socket (framing reused from the 090 IPC contract, not a second protocol)

- [ ] Plugin crash â†’ Core survives â†’ restart/disable path exercised in test

- [ ] Health states reported (HEALTHY/ENABLED/DISABLED/TRIAL per Â§10 Phase 4 vocabulary, forward-compatible)

- [ ] Core-owned capability IDs rejected when a manifest tries to claim them

- [ ] Level B plugin rules compiled into cached fast matcher ahead of time; asserted no-synchronous-execution by test (decision callback never blocks on plugin IPC: marker/timeout probe fails the suite if the callback thread waits)



Plan refs: Â§3.6 (PluginType, layout, hooks), Â§2 Data Flow steps 3/7, Â§7.2 Plugins page, Â§10 Phase 2.

title: Observe: the page's only control refuses, and it could not render truthfully
description:
The Observe page declares exactly two things: a button bound to `core.setObserve` and a `traceList` over `core:traces`. The button refuses in words on every build — `core.setObserve` is in `UNBOUND_ACTIONS` (`app/frontend/src/controls/actions.ts:222-229`) because there is no `Service.SetObserve` — and the page's own note calls itself "The live feed" (`app/backend/pages.go:151`) while being a 5s poll of a 200-row tail.

Even once bridged the toggle could not render truthfully. `core.setObserve` is a working daemon handler that flips the recorder's dry-run (`core/cmd/crossos/main.go:424-433`, and it deliberately does not default: `Enabled *bool`, nil refused), but `Recorder.DryRun()` has no read verb, so the control would be a blind fire-and-forget with no way to show the current state.

The rest of the recorder is built and unbridged: four Modes (`ModeOff`/`ModeMetadataOnly`/`ModeDebug`/`ModeFullTrace`, `core/pkg/record/record.go:21-24`) settable only in-process, `Recorder.Clear()` with no verb, and `Replay(ReplayTier)` (`record.go:205`) plus the whole replay/mismatch debug loop. For a product that records every keystroke decision, the absence of any recording-privacy control is a notable omission.
design:
`Service.SetObserve(on bool)` plus a read — `ObserveState` returning `{dryRun, mode}` — is the whole minimum.

`Service.SetObserve(on bool)` is correct as a Go signature precisely because it cannot be omitted, and that is what preserves the daemon's fail-closed contract. `core/cmd/crossos/main.go:424-433` takes `Enabled *bool` and rejects a payload that leaves it nil, commented: "Required, not defaulted: a payload missing the flag must not be read as 'stop observing' (or 'start') — the toggle the user pressed and the toggle that took effect have to be the same one." Keep the required field on the daemon side and make the Service method take a plain `bool`; do not add a default anywhere in between. The read half is the same shape and must report the recorder's ACTUAL `DryRun()` and `Mode()` (`core/pkg/record/record.go:68,82`) rather than the value the frontend last sent, or the toggle renders a state nobody read.

The mode question is a product decision, not a build detail: the recorder already redacts text/content/template/password/secret/clipboard at `ModeMetadataOnly` (`record.go:143-185`, the six keys at :143-146) and deliberately re-reads nothing pre-redaction. What the surface must say is what each mode buys, not what it is.

**There is no proven push architecture to extend.** The bus is not a precedent: `Bus.Subscribe` (`core/pkg/event/bus.go:38`) is called nowhere in the repository — I grepped, and the definition is the only hit. The daemon feeds the recorder by a direct `c.rec.OnOutcome(out)` on the decision path (`core/cmd/crossos/main.go:316`), so `core.traceWait`'s push shape has to be BUILT, not copied. The only proven live-wire pattern in the tree is the switcher's bounded long poll over IPC (`Service.SwitcherWait`, service.go:198).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Service.SetObserve(on bool) calls the daemon verb `core.setObserve` with the flag set from the argument — the plain `bool` is what makes the omission impossible — and Service.ObserveState returns the recorder's ACTUAL `DryRun()` and `Mode()`, read from the Recorder (`core/pkg/record/record.go:82` and `:68`), never a value the shell optimistically set. A state it has not read is never reported. The read half needs a daemon verb: `core.setObserve` is the only recorder verb registered (`core/cmd/crossos/main.go:859`), so this bead registers the read beside `handleSetObserve` in the same method table.
- [ ] `core.setObserve` leaves `UNBOUND_ACTIONS` and is served by `ACTION_COMMANDS` instead, with no narrow — and BOTH unbound entries go, not one. `app/frontend/src/controls/actions.ts:222` keys on the assembled `OBSERVE` constant and `:226` on the literal `'observe.set'` — the same daemon verb listed twice with identical `what` and `waitsOn`. Moving `[OBSERVE]` into `ACTION_COMMANDS` while leaving `'observe.set'` behind still satisfies the action gate (renderers.test.tsx:211-215) and changes nothing else, because `commandFor` checks ACTION_COMMANDS first (actions.ts:296-303). Delete the `'observe.set'` entry in the same commit.
- [ ] The mode is SURFACED, not settable. Service.ObserveState reports `Recorder.Mode()` and the copy below names what each mode buys; NO setter is added. There is no daemon verb for the mode (core/cmd/crossos/main.go:859 registers `core.setObserve` and nothing else), `Recorder.SetMode` (record.go:61) has no IPC entry, and the page that lets a person change one is a later bead — see "Not in this bead" below. Adding a setter here would be a new daemon verb this bead does not scope.
- [ ] Both new Service methods are added to the frozen list in `TestServiceExposesFrozenSources` (app/backend/uisources_test.go:457-476); its loop at :488-492 fails any bound method absent from that list, under ci.yml:42.
- [ ] A test asserts the Observe button's rendered label tracks ObserveState across two reads, so a fire-and-forget toggle cannot pass.
- [ ] The page's own copy stops lying, in one edit. `app/backend/pages.go:151` labels the trace control "The live feed" while the control is a 5s poll of a 200-row tail (`core/cmd/crossos/pagedata.go:1105` caps the rows; `app/frontend/src/App.tsx:273` sets the 5s interval). The replacement states that the feed is polled and how far back it reaches, and names ModeOff / ModeMetadataOnly / ModeDebug / ModeFullTrace and what each redacts. `app/backend/pages_test.go:376` pins the control's `kind` and the action, not this note, so the change is free. Leaving the string is leaving the diagnosis as decoration — this bead's whole thesis is that a control must not show a state the user has not been told how fresh it is.
- [ ] The new verbs are added to the `shellCalls` list at `core/cmd/crossos/main_test.go:880`, which already carries `core.setObserve` but does not carry the new read verb. That list is hand-kept and already stale — it omits `core.fileTypes`, `core.setFileType`, `core.reorderFileTypes` and `core.setMenuItemEnabled` (all registered at main.go:866-870) — so a method the shell starts calling is invisible to it unless the name is added. This is the Go-side counterpart to the vitest action gate at renderers.test.tsx:211-215. LANE: that file is run by ci.yml:40 (the CORE lane), not ci.yml:42, and ci.yml:40 is red today with 8 standing failures owned by cross-os-qji. This bead blocks on cross-os-qji, or a red in this criterion is not attributable to this change.
- [ ] REVIEWER NOTE: the two vitest criteria above — the Observe button's rendered label tracking ObserveState, and the action-registry gate that the `'observe.set'` duplicate would survive — are enforced by nothing today. No workflow in `.github/workflows` installs node, and `scripts/dev-verify.sh:172-190` runs only `npx tsc --noEmit`, skipping even that when node_modules (:175-178) or the generated Wails bindings (:179-182) are absent. The Go criteria split across TWO lanes: the frozen list and the `pages.go:151` copy are enforced by ci.yml:42; the `shellCalls` list is enforced by ci.yml:40 and is red for reasons this bead does not own. This bead's primary deliverable has a behavioural half only a vitest render test can reach, and that half is unwatched. Quote in the PR which half you ran; the full note is on cross-os-vrx.

Not in this bead — prohibitions and deferrals, not deliverables. None of these is ticked, and none is a criterion:
- `core.traceWait` and the trace inspector, including the toolbar a Clear button would sit on. There is no bus subscription to build on (see the design) and the switcher's bounded long poll is the only proven pattern; the page keeps polling for now. Clearing goes with it: `Recorder.Clear()` exists (core/pkg/record/record.go:135) and no daemon verb reaches it, so a `core.tracesClear` id with no trace view to clear from is a button that resolves to nothing, and the action gate would only require it be registered, not useful. The gap is recorded here as a decision, not an oversight.
- The page that SHOWS the modes and lets a person change one. There is no `core.settings` page in `CorePages()` — `core.settings` appears only as a fixture in `app/backend/shell_test.go:33`, not as a shipped page — so the selector has nowhere to live. That page, its sections and its privacy selector are one later bead, and this bead's ObserveState is the data source it will consume. The mode is READ here and SET there.
- `Recorder.Replay` / the replay-mismatch debug loop (`record.Replay(ReplayTier)` at record.go:205, `observe.Reproduce`/`Mismatch`). The bead names it as built and unbridged; this does not change that.
- Any redaction-policy change. The recorder already redacts at `ModeMetadataOnly` and deliberately re-reads nothing pre-redaction; this bead reports the mode in words and does not alter what is redacted.

# CI license/attribution merge gate (.github/workflows): Section 9.11 gate as a required job

## Background
Section 9.11 defines a load-bearing merge gate for any PR containing reused OSS code (pinned commit, license verified, transitive deps checked, copyright/NOTICE + ATTRIBUTION entry, merge) but no bead implements it as CI. Without automation the gate is advisory and GPL/no-license code can slip into the MIT core. Section 10 Phase 5 CI item and Section 11 merge-gate note both point here.

- CrossOS is MIT: GPL/copyleft and no-license sources can never pass (Section 9.11). A required CI job that fails closed (missing pin/license/attribution means fail) is the only enforcement that survives scale.

- Required GitHub Actions job: detects reused-OSS files in the diff, asserts pinned commit + license-verified (not GPL/copyleft/no-license) + transitive-dep check + copyright/NOTICE + ATTRIBUTION.md entry present and well-formed
- Fail-closed on missing data; human-readable rejection citing the Section 9.11 gate step

## Pass criteria
- [ ] PR adding an MIT file with pinned commit + LICENSE + NOTICE + ATTRIBUTION.md entry passes (positive fixture)
- [ ] PR adding unattributed / GPL-licensed / no-license code fails with the correct gate-step message (fixture PRs)
- [ ] Job is required (blocks merge) on push + PR
